title: Direct conversion of adult fibroblasts into motor neurons
protocol: Culture HEK293T cells in HEK culture medium one week before starting the preparation of viruses.
Pass HEK293T cells at about 80% confluency twice.
Seed about 8 × 10^6 HEK cells in 10 mL medium for each 10 cm plate.
Gently mix well to ensure cells distribute evenly on the surface.
Incubate until cell density reaches approximately 80% confluency for transfection.
Add 4 μg of plasmid#1 or plasmid#2, 2 μg of pMDLg/pRRE plasmid, 1 μg of pMD2.G plasmid, and 0.5 μg of pRSV-Rev plasmid to 1 mL DMEM (-FBS) media.
Add 22.5 μL transfection reagent PEI (1 μg/μL) to the plasmids mixture.
Mix well by gently pipetting up and down 5 times or vortexing for 15 s.
Incubate at room temperature for 15–20 min.
Add 1 mL of transfection dropwise to each 10 cm plate of HEK293 cells and gently mix to distribute the reagent evenly.
Replace with 10 mL HEK culture medium after 8 h transfection or overnight.
Collect lentiviral supernatant completely (around 10 mL) at 48 h post-transfection.
Add 10 mL fresh culture medium and store the collected supernatant at 4°C.
Collect lentiviral supernatant again after another 24 h (72 h post-transfection).
Store this second collection of lentiviral supernatant at 4°C.
Discard plates in a biohazard bag and autoclave it before disposal.
Pool two collections of the same lentivirus together.
Add 6 μg/mL polybrene to the pooled viral supernatants.
Filter the viral supernatants with 0.45 μm vacuum filters.
Store filtered viral supernatants at 4°C for up to two weeks or freeze at -80°C for long-term storage.
Seed HEK cells in a 24-well plate at a density of 7–10 × 10^4 cells/well/0.5 mL medium.
Make a serial dilution (e.g., 1:10, 1:100) of viral supernatant with HEK culture medium.
Add 50 μL of undiluted and diluted lentivirus to desired wells.
Set one well as a negative control without transduction.
Change the medium after 8 h or overnight (∼16 h) exposure to lentivirus.
Check the percentage of positive cells after 48–72 hours.
Quickly thaw a frozen stock of human fibroblast in a 37°C water bath.
Transfer cells into a 15 mL tube containing 5 mL of fibroblast culture medium and gently mix when ice is nearly gone.
Centrifuge at 200 g for 3 min to collect cells.
Remove the supernatant and resuspend cell pellet into 10 mL fibroblast culture medium.
Seed cells in one 10 cm plate.
Change media every two or three days until close to full confluency.
Wash the cells with 1× PBS when splitting fibroblasts.
Detatch cells by trypsinization with 0.05% trypsin at 37°C for 4 min.
Dilute Matrigel at 1:100 with cold DMEM medium.
Add 5 mL of diluted Matrigel to each 10 cm plate and gently shake to ensure coverage of the bottom surface.
Incubate the plates at 37°C for more than 3 hours or overnight.
Harvest fibroblasts at about 90% confluency by trypsinization.
Seed approximately 1 × 10^6 cells onto a Matrigel-coated 10 cm plate.
Mix the desired volume of two lentiviruses (1:1) in the presence of 6 μg/mL polybrene.
Add proper amount of lentivirus mixture to the plate to transduce fibroblasts.
Replace the media with fresh fibroblast medium the next morning after overnight exposure to lentiviruses.
Change the neural induction medium the day after replacing the fibroblast medium.
Change half volume of neural induction medium every other day at 4, 6, 8, 10, and 12 days post-infection (dpi).
Isolate mouse astrocytes from postnatal day 1 (P1) pups.
Culture astrocyte cells in DMEM with 15% FBS.
Prepare frozen stocks at ∼1 × 10^6 cells/vial.
Thaw astrocytes frozen stocks and culture them in astrocyte culture media in 10 cm cell culture plates.
Seed cells from one vial of frozen stock (1 × 10^6 cells) on one 10 cm plate.
Culture until around 90% confluency is reached.
Coat 24-well plates contain cover slips with Matrigel (1:100) at least for 3 h in 37°C.
Trypsinize astrocytes with 0.025% trypsin for 3 min at 37°C when cells reach ∼90% confluency.
Add astrocyte medium to neutralize trypsin and detach cells.
Transfer cell suspension to a 15 mL tube and centrifuge at 200 g for 3 min to collect cells.
Resuspend the cell pellet into 12 mL astrocyte medium.
Seed astrocytes onto coverslips in a 24-well plate at 0.5 mL/well.
Change medium every two days until astrocytes form monolayer on coverslips.
Add 10 μM Ara-C in culture medium if astrocytes reach full confluency before neurons are ready for replating.
Coat culture plates with 5 mL of 0.1% gelatin for 30 min at 37°C.
Remove culture medium from culture plates with induced neurons and wash once with PBS.
Add 3 mL of 0.025% trypsin to a 10 cm plate and incubate for 3 min at 37°C.
Quench trypsin activity by adding 7 mL fibroblast culture medium.
Gently pipette up and down to break cell aggregates.
Transfer cell suspension to gelatin-coated plates (about 5 mL each).
Incubate plates at 37°C and check the attachment of cells under microscope.
Collect cell suspensions and transfer to a 15 mL tube.
Pool cell suspensions from two plates together.
Centrifuge at 300 g for 3 min to collect cells.
Remove the supernatant and gently resuspend the cell pellets into neural maturation medium with desired volume based on yield and experimental plans.
Seed neurons generated from one 10 cm plate into a 24-well plate with a density of ∼2 × 10^4 cells/well.
Fix cultured cells with 4% paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS for 15 min at room temperature.
Wash fixed cells twice with PBS.
Incubate fixed cells in blocking buffer (PBS containing 0.2% Triton X-100 and 3% BSA) for 1 h at room temperature for permeabilization and blocking.
Incubate cells with primary antibodies in blocking buffer at 4°C overnight (∼16 h).
Wash coverslips with PBS for 10 min × 4 after removal of primary antibodies.
Incubate coverslips with corresponding fluorophore-conjugated secondary antibodies in the dark at room temperature for 2 h.
Wash coverslips with PBS for 10 min × 3.
Stain nuclei with Hoechst 33342 (1:3000) in PBS at room temperature for 15 min.
Briefly wash coverslips once with PBS.
Mount coverslips with mounting medium on microslides.
Air dry the coverslips and visualize cells under a confocal microscope.
